title: Modularize performance harness: split load, regression, and eval pipelines
creator: Maya Chen
description: Refactor and modularize our benchmarking and testing harness to reduce flakiness, speed up iteration, and make performance/regression/eval suites independently maintainable. Current problems: (1) Monolithic test runner mixes load testing (k6/locust) with perf regression checks and the Python eval pipeline, causing long CI times and fragile coupling. (2) Out-of-date dependencies (k6 image, torch 2.1 micro-updates, numpy) cause reproducibility issues across CI agents. (3) KV cache warmup logic is duplicated across suites and is source of intermittent regressions. Goals: split into three focused components (load-runner, perf-regression, eval-pipeline), provide a lightweight compatibility shim for older artifacts, pin and modernize dependencies, and add stable baselining and synthetic traffic generators so we can detect regressions earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Load tests run independently in dedicated CI workflow and complete within target wall time (<= 25m for full suite)
Perf regression suite produces deterministic token-level latency percentiles and stores baselines in s3://redwood-perf/baselines/{model}/{tag}
Eval pipeline is packaged as a small Python wheel and can be invoked locally (./bin/run-evals) and inside CI container with pinned deps
KV cache warmup logic is extracted to shared library and used by all three harnesses with unit tests
CI flakiness rate for perf/eval tests reduced by >= 60% (measured by flaky test reruns in last 30 days)
notes: This ticket is primarily refactor/cleanup but touches infra (CI images) and runtime hooks. We must coordinate with infra and release teams for image upgrades and rollout. There is risk around dependency upgrades that could alter perf curves; we will gate those changes behind perf regression runs against canary models.
design_decisions: Adopt modular directory layout: /harness/load, /harness/regression, /harness/eval; shared libs under /harness/common
Keep k6 for high-throughput synthetic load but containerize a minimal locust runner for developer local runs
Package eval pipeline as wheel with explicit entrypoints to avoid PYTHONPATH issues in CI
Pin torch to 2.1.x where we run quantized kernels; upgrade numpy to 1.26 and add compatibility shims for older arrays
tradeoffs: Shipping wheel for evals adds build step to release pipeline but simplifies local reproducibility
Pinning torch to 2.1.x may delay taking advantage of upstream 2.2 perf improvements; we'll measure 2.2 in a parallel branch before upgrading
Splitting pipelines increases number of CI jobs (more parallelism) which may raise CI minutes - offset by faster per-job completion and better caching
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Create modular repo layout and shared common/kv_warmup library (branch: ENG-8392/module-layout)
Phase 2: Extract and containerize load runner; add dedicated CI workflow 'perf-load' (concurrent with phase 1)
Phase 3: Package eval pipeline as wheel, pin dependencies, add smoke tests and local runner script
Phase 4: Migrate perf regression jobs to new runner; add baseline storage and comparison tool (s3 upload + dashboard link)
Phase 5: Run canary against staging models, collect metrics, roll out image upgrades once baselines are stable
risks_mitigation: Risk: Dependency upgrade changes latency profiles. Mitigation: run controlled A/B perf tests and preserve old baselines for rollback
Risk: CI minute increase. Mitigation: gate full runs to nightly and provide faster smoke suites for PRs
Risk: Shared library regressions. Mitigation: unit tests + canary runs and feature-flagged deployment of shared lib
